svg.title: Aircraft documents: what PHAK says about the paperwork
svg.desc: The Certificate of Aircraft Registration must be carried in the aircraft at all times. The Airworthiness Certificate must be displayed legibly to passengers and crew and stays with the aircraft. Pilots must comply with the operating limitations in the approved AFM, markings and placards. The AFM/POH Section 6 holds weight and balance information; part 91 has no specified requirement to calculate it before every flight, but the pilot in command must comply with the AFM limits, which include weight and balance. The owner must keep the documents current.
svg.text: Aircraft documents: what PHAK says about the paperwork
The registration certificate, airworthiness certificate, operating limitations (AFM/POH) and weight
and balance information, each as PHAK states it.
Certificate of Aircraft Registration
Before flight the aircraft must be registered
with the FAA Aircraft Registry
The certificate is issued to the owner as
evidence of registration and must be carried in
the aircraft at all times
Cannot be used for operations when: registered
under foreign law; registration canceled on
written request; aircraft destroyed or scrapped;
ownership transferred; holder loses U.S.
citizenship
Pink copy of Form 8050-1: may operate an
unregistered aircraft for no more than 90 days,
not outside the United States
Airworthiness Certificate
Issued by an FAA representative after the
aircraft is inspected, meets 14 CFR part 21 and
is in condition for safe operation
Must be displayed so it is legible to passengers
and crew whenever the aircraft is operated
Must remain with the aircraft unless it is sold
to a foreign purchaser
Standard: in effect indefinitely if the aircraft
is maintained under parts 21, 43 and 91 and is
registered in the U.S.
Special: for Experimental, Restricted, Limited,
Provisional and Light-Sport Aircraft
Operating limitations and the AFM/POH
AFM: written by the manufacturer, approved by the
FAA, specific to a make and model, usually by
serial number
Part 91 requires the pilot to comply with the
operating limitations in the approved flight
manuals, markings and placards
The title page must show the serial number and
registration; without them the manual is for
general study only
Section 2, Limitations: airspeed, powerplant,
weight and loading distribution, flight limits,
placards
The owner/information manual is not FAA approved
and cannot be substituted for the AFM/POH
Weight and balance
AFM/POH Section 6, Weight and Balance/Equipment
List: all the information the FAA requires to
calculate weight and balance
Section 2 gives the maximum certificated weights,
the CG range and the datum location
Part 91 has no specified requirement to do weight
and balance calculations before each flight, but
section 91.9 requires the pilot in command to
comply with the AFM operating limits, and these
include weight and balance
Still, before any flight the pilot should
determine the weight and balance condition
Weight changes must be noted in the weight and
balance records and the equipment list updated,
if appropriate
The registered owner/operator is responsible for having a current Airworthiness Certificate and a
Certificate of Aircraft Registration in the aircraft
A current FCC radio station license is needed if equipped with radios (including the ELT) and operated
outside the United States
